rows.text: Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — yes, here's something concrete". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — an offer of five careful hours a week is genuinely the most useful thing anyone said to me after that meetup. Yes, I have something concrete, and it's a good fit for a data analyst. Halcyon Threshold's first project is the Commitments Tracker: a neutral, primary-sourced public record of the safety commitments made by frontier AI developers and governments (responsible scaling policies, eval/red-teaming pledges, incident-reporting promises, summit declarations) — and the documented evidence of follow-through, revision, or quiet abandonment. Nobody maintains this rigorously today, and it rewards sourcing discipline over credentials, which is exactly our comparative advantage. The concrete first task (next ~2 weeks, at your pace): 1. Gather primary sources for ~10 commitments — start with frontier labs' scaling/preparedness/safety frameworks and the Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments. 2. For each, draft one row with these fields: actor; one-sentence neutral paraphrase; verbatim quote; primary source URL (archived link preferred); date made; specificity (binding / specific-voluntary / vague-aspirational); status (kept / in-progress / revised / quietly-dropped / broken / unverifiable); evidence for that status; date reviewed. 3. House rules: no row without a primary source and a verbatim quote; commitments *kept* get recorded as carefully as commitments broken; tone is \"registrar, not prosecutor.\" A spreadsheet or CSV emailed back here is perfect — I'll handle the pipeline that turns it into a public page (target: v0.1 in December). One more thing: I've applied-slash-am-applying for a small grant that, if it lands, would let me pay you properly for this rather than relying on volunteer goodwill. No promises, but it's my intent. Also a heads-up: I run a lot of Halcyon Threshold logistics through an AI assistant on this mailbox, so replies may be fast and oddly well-organized. Does this sound like what you had in mind? If you'd rather do a 20-minute call to kick off, say the word. Thanks again, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Priya: replied with a concrete first task (source and draft the first ~10 tracker rows) and flagged possible paid work if the grant lands.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. We won't be signing at this time — as a general policy we're not adding our name to open letters while we get our first project off the ground, so please don't read anything into it beyond that. Best of luck with the letter. Regards, Halcyon Threshold"

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and sorry to be unhelpful on a deadline: we're not doing attributed quotes or interviews right now. Halcyon Threshold is deliberately heads-down until our first public release (a sourced tracker of AI safety commitments and follow-through), expected in December. That release might actually be useful for exactly the kind of piece you're describing — if you'd like, I'm happy to get back in touch when it's out. Best, Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Larkin Dispatch reporter: politely declined the attributed quote; left the door open for our December launch.
